html:
Liberia's open register of ships, set up in 1948 with American help, which lets owners anywhere fly the Liberian flag, with low fees and light rules. It is the best-known flag of convenience.

The register was designed by a company linked to former US Secretary of State Edward Stettinius and is run from Virginia, not Monrovia. It grew fast, and by the 1960s Liberia had one of the largest merchant fleets in the world by tonnage, a rank it still holds alongside Panama. The fees were a steady income for the state, even during the civil wars. Critics say such flags let owners avoid labour and safety rules. See also William Tubman and the law of the sea.
